_why: The ONE table both implementations are checked against. Swift decides what the daemon serves; docpath.js decides what the page requests. A disagreement is a silently broken image, so neither side gets to hold its own copy of the cases.

vectors.why: a document at the worktree root needs no prefix
parent traversal resolves against the document's directory
a leading / means worktree-root-relative, not filesystem-absolute
DRIFT #1: WebKit decodes url.path, so an encoded allowlist entry could never match
percent-decoding is not limited to spaces
a query is not part of the path
a fragment is not part of the path
remote: the CSP blocks it and the daemon never serves it
inline: the page renders it without asking anyone
DRIFT #2: RFC 3986 schemes start with a LETTER, so this is an oddly-named file
